title: Prayer in the Church
definition: Prayer in the Church is the gathered and continual dependence of God's people on the Father through Christ by the Holy Spirit.
summary: The Church lives and serves by prayerful dependence on God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gives His people access to the Father and intercedes for them as they pray.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Prayer in the Church teaches that Christ does not redeem people into isolation but into a gathered, accountable, worshiping, serving, and mission-shaped people. The Church belongs to Jesus, is formed by the Gospel, and is strengthened by the Word, prayer, ordinances, fellowship, and Spirit-empowered service.

This doctrine helps believers see the Church as more than a place to attend. It is the household of God, the body of Christ, and a visible witness to the grace, holiness, unity, and truth of the Lord.

The specific emphasis here is the church lives and serves by prayerful dependence on god.. A healthy church life displays Christ's care for His people and His mission to the world.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because many people treat church as optional, consumer-driven, or disconnected from discipleship. Prayer in the Church calls believers back to Christ's design for His people, where worship, truth, love, accountability, service, and mission are held together.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Participate in church life with humility and faithfulness. Let prayer in the church move you to serve, forgive, gather, pray, give, submit to Scripture, care for others, and help the body of Christ grow in love and maturity.
